summary: mymatasan cameras now verify credentials against the device before they are ever persisted: adding a discovered camera (or updating its saved credentials) resolves the ONVIF stream URI and/or probes RTSP DESCRIBE with the supplied login, and a camera that actively rejects it (401/403, or the 400+NotAuthorized fault many ONVIF cameras use for a bad WS-Security digest) is refused with a clear error instead of being saved with dead credentials; an unreachable camera is still allowed through since that is not proof of a bad password. A new GET /api/cameras/{id}/auth-check re-verifies a saved camera's stored credentials on demand, and the camera node's UI now blocks all tabs behind a centered credential-entry gate the moment stored credentials stop authenticating (e.g. after an out-of-band password change on the camera itself). Added a full ONVIF Device-Management surface per camera: list/create/delete local ONVIF user accounts, reboot, factory default (soft/hard), camera clock (manual or NTP) read/write, and network (IPv4/gateway/DNS) read/write, all gated by a new GET /api/cameras/{id}/capabilities that actually probes each read call (GetUsers/GetSystemDateAndTime/GetNetwork) since these operations share one mandatory ONVIF service and can't otherwise be told apart per-firmware — so the Settings UI only shows management boxes the camera genuinely supports. GET /api/cameras/{id}/device-info surfaces manufacturer/model/firmware/serial/MAC address/ONVIF version/location for a new Live View 'Camera Information' panel. A specific detected stream (from Discover) can now be live-previewed and connectivity-tested without persisting anything, so probing an alternate profile never disturbs the camera's active recording/detection stream. Separately, the Alert Log grid was rewired onto the shared DataTable's new server mode: every column filter and sort now runs as a true DB-side query (domain/shared/apis query-option parsing gained float64 filter support for the Confidence column) instead of a client-side slice over a fixed date window, so it stays fast over large detection histories; it defaults to the latest detections with a one-click 'Today' filter.
compatibility: Existing saved cameras and their stored credentials are unaffected; verification only runs on new saves/credential updates and the new on-demand auth-check endpoint. The legacy GET /api/vision/alerts query params (createdAfter/createdBefore/ruleId/detectionType) were replaced by the generic filters/sorters JSON pair shared with other list endpoints — any external script or dashboard calling those exact params must switch to the new filters/sorters contract; cameraId and status params are unchanged. DataTable's new serverMode is opt-in per usage (default remains client-side filtering), so other tables in mymatasan/myidsan/myseliasan are unaffected.
